title: Beyond the 956: Tony Richards, original W.A.S.P. drummer, dies at 69
excerpt: Tony Richards, the original drummer of 1980s heavy metal band W.A.S.P., has died at 69. The band announced his death on November 11, 2026; no cause of death was shared.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tony Richards, the original drummer of the 1980s heavy metal band W.A.S.P., has died at 69.

W.A.S.P. announced his death on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in a statement from the band's founder and frontman, Blackie Lawless, shared on the band's official social media. USA Today confirmed the death on November 13. No cause of death was shared, and no exact date of death was given.

Born Anthony Richard Orlando on June 19, 1957, in Phoenix, Arizona, Richards was one of the four founding members of W.A.S.P., formed in Los Angeles in 1982. He played drums on the band's self-titled debut album, which included “I Wanna Be Somebody,” “L.O.V.E. Machine” and “Sleeping (In the Fire),” and left the group shortly after. Before W.A.S.P., he played in Dante Fox, the Los Angeles band that later became Great White.

Lawless remembered Richards as an equal among the band's founders, writing, “Tony was absolutely equal to any of the others that were in the Band. His personality was infectious.” He said watching Richards play live left audiences “riveted … no matter where you were in the room,” and that his departure left the band “wounded in a way that we never really quite recovered from.” Former guitarist Chris Holmes also paid tribute on November 12, writing that Richards “deserved not to be forgotten along with what he brought to this industry.”

Richards is the third former W.A.S.P. drummer to die, after Frankie Banali in 2020 and Steve Riley in 2023. He is survived by his brother, John.

Rest in Peace, Tony Richards.

Sources: USA Today; W.A.S.P. (official band statement); Noise11; Lambgoat.
